steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: Ugh, took a peltin' and some. Missed Captain Kelly in the end.

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: Here, take this hankie, wipe yourself off, or else the smell of those rotten leaves'll stick to you.

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: Thank you!

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: Didn't imagine any of our soldiers apart from Captain Kelly would visit District Seventeen on their own.

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: Our soldiers? You mean like, you're one too?

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: Shh.

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: (Clears throat) I slipped out in secret. Can't do that in uniform.

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: You're not gonna make anyone happy taking a shortcut to the barracks through here in that getup.

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: Eh, really?

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: No wonder. I barely said anythin' before it was a bombardment of all gone-off leaves and fruit.

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: Are you a new transfer?

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: Kind of. I'm here from Londinium.

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: Well, Londinium! I've never been. Must be miles larger than County Hillock there...

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: Does The Shard really go three hundred floors up? Is there really a teleportation circle buried in the mound under the Royal Victorian Academy of Sciences, leading to the miraculous space where the first Draco King's Jewels are kept?

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: Eh... eh? Jewels? Never even heard of them.

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: But I do know what the high-speed terrestrial warships look like when they leave the factory, and I've seen the hydroponics workshop... If you wanna know anythin' of that sort, I could definitely tell you.

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: Warships? Hydroponics workshop...? Doesn't sound... too much like Londinium is in novels... Oh! Sorry! Don't let me distract you.

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: If you want to investigate, it'll probably be hard to ask on any of these streets.

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: Might end up like this again, with...

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: With gettin' a stink all over me for no reason?

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: Got off light, haha. You're not that stinky.

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: Do these residents often have clashes with us soldiers?

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: Used to just be minor friction, but it's been getting tenser lately.

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: It's like you've been hearing. There's been several cases of our soldiers getting targeted in attacks, and it's stretching everyone's nerves close to the limit—

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: Could it really be the spectre force... that's weird, they didn't really target ordinary soldiers before.

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: Spectre... what are you going on about?

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: ...Nothin'.

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: Speakin' of, that patrol just now callin' the people here 'Tara rabble'—

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: Hold on, don't—don't just say that out loud here! They'll be eyeing us again... What, are you hoping to take away even more rotten veg?

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: Ah... gotcha. Are they really not Victorians?

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: Of course they're Victorians.

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: I'm gettin' more and more lost here.

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: Some people would choose another word, yeah, the one you've been hearing—Tarans, that's their identity.

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: You have both the locals themselves who would call them that, as well as a decent portion of the soldiers.

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: Now that you put a fine point on it, I've heard the term before.

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: In novels?

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: In history textbooks.

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: Right. They've always been here.

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: Over hundreds of years ago, when it wasn't County Hillock yet, and we still hadn't built our nomadic cities, back when it was grass all across the vales as far as the eye could see, this place was their home.

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: I still remember the legend of the Draco King, Gaeil... was he born right around here?

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: Tara was the very name of this region back then.

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: Right. I've read heaps of novels all about the saga of King Gaeil.

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: King Gaeil led the Tarans in a conflict against the first Aslan King, but a few years later, he signed a peace treaty along with the ruler of Londinium, didn't he?

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: And here I was thinkin', after that, the word Tara just sort of fell away.

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: Before I came to County Hillock, I thought the same...

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: But Victoria's always changing, isn't it? Us Vouivre didn't always live here, but we're all Victorian citizens now.

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: If everyone's minds went like that, we'd avoid plenty of conflict.

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: *Sigh*...

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: No need to let it get you down, though. The whole reason we're here is to uncover the real enemy, stop the clash gettin' any bigger, isn't it?

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: So you'd rather not leave, even if it means a headful of rotten cabbage?

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: Haha, you think I'm bein' a right dunce, don't you?

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: No, not at all. Actually, you're amazing to me.

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: The patrol just now, I've seen masses of rough attitude like that. It's not like I've never wanted to stop it... but I'm a guard of honor, that's all I am.

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: And what's so bad about that? You're a member of Victoria's army too. Course you've got the power to change the situation, if it doesn't sit right with you!

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: Do... do I really?

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: Oh, thank you... you're the first person who's ever told me that. Yeah, next time, I'll give it a go...

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: Oh, yeah, is there anything else I can help you with? Apart from picking these leaves off you... after all, I don't want to see this conflict boil over either.

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: Let me think... d'you have any local friends you ken? I want to ask whereabouts Damian Barry usually went.

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: Friends I've got... Saoirse might know something.

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: Give me a way to keep in touch, and I'll visit the newspaper in a moment. Don't think the Sergeant Major would mind if I'm missing today...

steps.name: Colonel Hamilton
steps.text: Skamandros.

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: Colonel.

steps.name: Colonel Hamilton
steps.text: I once saw your father—over twenty years ago, at a ball the Duke of Caster was holding. Of course, I was still a bottom-rung guard then, so all I had was a glimpse from afar at the White Wolf Count of legend.

steps.name: Colonel Hamilton
steps.text: Not long after, I heard a deformed feathered reptile struck illness into him at a Londinium beastlife garden, and he quickly took leave from the aristocratic circles.

steps.name: Colonel Hamilton
steps.text: Ever since, he hasn't taken a step beyond his manor at Portsmouth City.

steps.name: Colonel Hamilton
steps.text: Is your father still in fine spirits?

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: Thank you for your concern, and I hope reminiscing over these years-old affairs hasn't eaten up too much of your precious time. After all, meeting with you doesn't prove easy.

steps.name: Colonel Hamilton
steps.text: You don't resemble your father.

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: As is clear, my father did not have the opportunity to serve for the Empire's Army like you or I do.

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: Considering the theft of these military Originium goods couldn't possibly relate to him, maybe we don't have a need for probing further into his later life.

steps.name: Colonel Hamilton
steps.text: One's background decides what kind of person one becomes. Would you agree with that, Skamandros?

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: I believe one has the right to choose one's own future.

steps.name: Colonel Hamilton
steps.text: Listen to that. How befitting an answer of your status.

steps.name: Colonel Hamilton
steps.text: The progeny of the Aslans' aide, first-class honors from the Royal Guard Academy, a Londinium army upstart—of course you believe you can change anything and everything.

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: I have no intent to make any such changes, Colonel. You don't need to worry about our squad potentially impacting your command over County Hillock...

steps.name: Colonel Hamilton
steps.text: For a joke, I don't find that humorous at all. You can't be so arrogant as to think I'd occupy myself with a paltry little lieutenant?

steps.name: Colonel Hamilton
steps.text: I've met people like you plenty. Always all braggadocio, skin-deep, and superficial. I deigned to meet you because I wanted to tell you this—

steps.name: Colonel Hamilton
steps.text: Don't interfere in things beyond your ken.

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: I'm sorry, I cannot agree to that.

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: The orders we received were to ascertain the lost Originium products' whereabouts.

steps.name: Colonel Hamilton
steps.text: If you just stay still and wait where you ought to, then before long, you may accomplish your duty and return to Londinium with all the ostentation you'd like.

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: I don't need that ostentation of yours, and Victoria needs it even less.

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: I'm not in the routine of reporting back with a hurriedly lopped-off head, sans trial.

steps.name: Colonel Hamilton
steps.text: Hahah! You're telling me I've a disregard for human life—and you believe those people are truly innocent? How ridiculous!

steps.name: Colonel Hamilton
steps.text: Just ten days ago, three of our soldiers were murdered in cold blood. James Cohen, Robert Boris, and Jeremy Brown.

steps.name: Colonel Hamilton
steps.text: When Cohen's wife wrote to tell him she was with a second child, she had no idea that her husband had had a hole gruesomely blown in his head.

steps.name: Colonel Hamilton
steps.text: Boris could've left this place once midsummer passed. He mentioned he'd go back to continue his family's clothiers after his retirement.

steps.name: Colonel Hamilton
steps.text: And Brown, he was a bright young student just a year ago, and not even twenty when he died!

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: I give my profound regrets for their sacrifice.

steps.name: Colonel Hamilton
steps.text: Regrets! Hah, what weightless rhetoric, just like every word that wafts out of your mouth.

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: This is exactly why all of us want to catch hold of the assassinators. Colonel, on this matter, we have held unanimous positions throughout.

steps.name: Colonel Hamilton
steps.text: No one else but that Tara rabble killed them. We've uncovered two already, but I know there are still more tucked in the background.

steps.name: Colonel Hamilton
steps.text: Fifteen days ago, our barracks suffered an explosive attack at three simultaneous places. An according fifteen soldiers lost their lives. The craters and the spilled blood of our own still lie where they were.

steps.name: Colonel Hamilton
steps.text: Twenty-one days ago, our resupply transport group were ambushed outside the distribution sector in the outskirts north, and the whole detachment together with their goods disappeared without a trace. Do you feel there is any possibility they would still be alive?

steps.name: Colonel Hamilton
steps.text: This is only the last month's events, to boot. You know nothing at all of the losses we've long since endured.

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: These incidents you mention all sound very in line with the spectre force's MO.

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: In the past half a year, Londinium has continually received reports from more than ten different counties, logging up to hundreds of homicide, looting and property damage cases.

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: After every offence, they swiftly conceal their tracks, and all connected personnel who've seen them are caught in assassinations before they can contact us.

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: We've been able to obtain exceedingly little information so far.

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: That is why the lead before us is so crucial.

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: We still don't know the spectre force's goal in haunting County Hillock, but I believe that they are our mutual enemy.

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: Colonel, if we and the barracks can cooperate, and uncover the spectre force here, it'll be of great benefit to County Hillock and Victoria as a whole.

steps.name: Colonel Hamilton
steps.text: Hmph. You still understand nothing at all. You treat the atrocities before you as just another case to win you a medal.

steps.name: Colonel Hamilton
steps.text: But you're wrong, soldier. This is not some case, and no such true culprit exists. This is a war, and it is between us and them, a war ongoing for decades, even for centuries.

steps.name: Colonel Hamilton
steps.text: You call them a spectre force, but do you know what that name signifies?

steps.name: Colonel Hamilton
steps.text: Who is the enemy we've been confronting all this time? Well?

steps.name: Colonel Hamilton
steps.text: It's a ghost! It's a phantom drifting over this city, an apparition that echoes in the heads of Taran morons, it is a life-in-spirit ghost!

steps.name: Colonel Hamilton
steps.text: And that spectre speaks a different language to us, willfully distorts the history molded by our ancestors' hands, has delusions that by the body of our city it will one day return to life!

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: Are you saying that a great amount of the local populace are supporters of the spectre force?

steps.name: Colonel Hamilton
steps.text: Great amount? Supporters? No, you're mistaken. They are one single whole.

steps.name: Colonel Hamilton
steps.text: Have you ever read this anthology of poetry?

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: Seamus Williams. His poems have some fame in Londinium too.

steps.name: Colonel Hamilton
steps.text: This is their very compilation of bare-faced lies about Victoria. In their depictions, they have their own language; they are this land's natural owners.

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: Still, Victoria can tolerate the mindsets of authors who come from differing cultural backgrounds.

steps.name: Colonel Hamilton
steps.text: No one would assume a dreamer's fantasy as their truth. Not unless that dream mentioned taking up a hatchet. Not unless it was about wanting to cut our heads off.

steps.name: Colonel Hamilton
steps.text: I still keep this book of an idiot's sleeptalk so that the bloodstains upon it always remind me—

steps.name: Colonel Hamilton
steps.text: If one lives on Victoria's land, yet refuses to give one's own name in Victorian, then one is no longer a Victorian, but an enemy and a menace to this country's safety!

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: You... you executed the holder of this anthology? Simply because they...

steps.name: Victorian Soldier
steps.text: Reporting in!

steps.name: Colonel Hamilton
steps.text: Speak.

steps.name: Victorian Soldier
steps.text: Command has lost contact with 9th Defence and 13th Defence after they were attacked.

steps.name: Victorian Soldier
steps.text: 5th, 7th and 10th Defence each sent vanguards ASAP to the scene, and did not find traces of the enemy.

steps.name: Colonel Hamilton
steps.text: What of our own?

steps.name: Victorian Soldier
steps.text: They... gave their lives.

steps.name: Colonel Hamilton
steps.text: Did you hear that, Skamandros?

steps.name: Colonel Hamilton
steps.text: Right as you were seeing fit to tell me sympathetic rubbish to the enemy, we once again saw outstanding soldiers die at their hands!

steps.name: Colonel Hamilton
steps.text: If that's gotten through your head, then kindly eject yourself from my office. I still have genuine work awaiting me.

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: Fine. Very fine. I have my own work to do too.
